name: Dao Duy Tu
role: Scholar barred from the Ming-era exam system for his family's hát xướng background; fled south, became chief strategist and advisor to chúa Nguyễn Phúc Nguyên, proposed and oversaw the Lũy Thầy defensive line
known_facts: Born 1572 in Thanh Hóa; barred from sitting the Đàng Ngoài exams because his family worked as hát xướng (theatrical/singing) performers, a stigmatized occupation

Went south to Đàng Trong and presented the poem 'Ngọa Long Cương' to chúa Nguyễn Phúc Nguyên, who honored him with the title 'Thầy' (Teacher) — the origin of the name 'Lũy Thầy' for the wall system he later proposed

In 1630, when Trịnh Tráng sent an edict demanding tribute and a son sent to court, devised the double-bottomed bronze tray (mâm đồng hai đáy) to return the edict without open confrontation, signaling Đàng Trong's refusal to submit
Proposed and directed the 1630 construction of Lũy Trường Dục, the first wall in the system, running from Núi Thần Đinh along sông Rào Đá to phá Hạc Hải
Died 17th day of the 10th lunar month, year Giáp Tuất, i.e. 7 December 1634, aged 63
His death and chúa Nguyễn Phúc Nguyên's death the following year (1635) left the walls he proposed to be maintained and tested by later generals, chiefly Nguyễn Hữu Dật
interpretation: Early 17th-century Vietnamese scholar-advisor in plain dark court dress, based on the user reference.
